title: Review of c06's pcell yield selection: replicated on seeds 5 and 6 against the neutral arm
summary: Re-ran c06's world.py and genealogy.py unchanged (nkinds=2, y2=0.7 and the neutral y2=1.0) on fresh seeds 5 and 6 to T=16000, plus a labkit pack of the y2=0.7 arm on seed 5 (world_y07.py only sets those defaults). The low-yield kind's share of particles in cells falls 0.418->0.09 and 0.548->0.145; the neutral arm drifts 0.473->0.537 and 0.497->0.564. Persistent splits from pure parents high/low yield: 2/0 and 6/0 (neutral: 1/0 and 0/1, most splits from mixed cells). Cell deaths 1-3 per run, all of mixed cells; one pure-cell conversion in y0.7 seed 5. The particles sheet shows cyan (kind 1) cells staying small while white cells grow and divide. The finding replicates, including its own caveat: colonization-phase selection with kinds assigned at seeding, not L7.

observations.H: rerun/seed5/particles.png t=4000-16000: cyan (low-yield) cells stay small, white cells grow and divide; data/g_y0.7_s5.json series: low-yield share in cells 0.418 -> 0.09 (seed 6: 0.548 -> 0.145)

controls_run.H: data/g_y1.0_s5.json, data/g_y1.0_s6.json (neutral arm y2=1.0, same seeds): share 0.473 -> 0.537, 0.497 -> 0.564

verdicts.limitation: As c06 states: kinds are assigned at seeding (50/50 per particle), cells purify by drift, and selection acts through differential growth and division with 1-3 deaths, all of mixed cells, so this is colonization-phase cell-level selection, not L7. Split counts per run are small (4-9 persistent). One pure-cell conversion occurred (y0.7 seed 5). I did not re-run the gate-off ablation.
